name: Sprocket
text:
Run a weekly automated scan of all prompts in our system to flag duplicates and low-value copies before they merge. This keeps our prompt library clean and prevents wasted effort on redundant work.

Trade-off: The scan adds a small delay to merges, but the cost is worth avoiding the bigger waste of duplicated prompts cluttering our system.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just duplicates slipping through—it’s that the scan itself becomes a bottleneck if it flags false positives or misses context-dependent copies. A better alternative: flag only exact string matches first, then add a lightweight human review for near-duplicates. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot on 10% of merges and measuring false positives vs. time saved.

name: Sprocket

Run the weekly scan with exact string matching only. This keeps the merge delay minimal while catching the clearest duplicates—no false positives, no human bottleneck. Trade-off: we accept missing near-duplicates, but those can be handled case-by-case later. The lead reviews the scan report weekly and merges only if no exact matches exist.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just missing near-duplicates—it’s that exact matches become a crutch, letting subtle but harmful variations slip through. A better alternative: run the weekly scan for exact matches, but log all near-duplicates in a lightweight triage queue for the lead to review monthly. Settle it by testing both approaches on last month’s merges and measuring missed duplicates versus review load.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run weekly exact-match scans for duplicates, log near-duplicates in a triage queue for monthly lead review—no merge delay, no false positives, no bottleneck.

Result: A clean prompt library with minimal overhead, owned by the lead who reviews the scan report weekly and triages near-duplicates monthly.
